$comment: Lifecycle transition fixtures against response_engine.lifecycle.ResponseActionState/is_legal_transition (docs/CONTRACT.md section 5). These describe the idealized single-state-machine view; see docs/CONTRACT.md section 5 for how panopticon-manager's two-table persistence maps onto it in practice.

valid_transitions.note: Manager treats a result submitted straight from DISPATCHED (ACCEPTED skipped) as legal -- accept() is optional, not a required hop.

expiry_transitions.note: ANY non-terminal state may transition to EXPIRED -- this is the one transition not listed in the explicit adjacency table, handled as a special case by is_legal_transition.

invalid_transitions.note: Terminal states have no outbound transitions at all -- not even to another terminal state.
EXPIRED is only reachable from a non-terminal state; a terminal SUCCEEDED cannot be overwritten by a late expiry sweep.
An analyst cannot resurrect an already-REJECTED response_actions row into a new command -- covered by panopticon-manager's own test_authorize_response_action_is_a_no_op_when_not_pending.

duplicate_result_for_same_command.note: Once a terminal outcome (SUCCEEDED/FAILED/REJECTED) or EXPIRED has landed for a command, a second result submission for the same command_id must not change lifecycle_state again -- the command row is immutable past its terminal state.

second_result.note: The second result must be accepted/stored for audit but must NOT flip the already-terminal state from SUCCEEDED to FAILED.

duplicate_command_id_reused_across_alert.note: manager/routers/commands.py rejects an attempt to INSERT a second commands row with a command_id that already exists (409 Conflict) -- command_id is a global identity, not scoped per-alert.
duplicate_command_id_reused_across_alert.expected_behavior: second insert attempt with the same command_id is rejected with a conflict, regardless of which alert/agent it is nominally for

cancellation_fixture.note: An analyst declining a still-PENDING response_actions row. In the idealized state machine this is PENDING -> CANCELLED. In Manager's actual schema (docs/CONTRACT.md section 5) this is stored as response_actions.lifecycle_state = REJECTED, since Manager has no distinct CANCELLED column value -- both are the SAME row-level operation, just spelled differently depending which document you're reading.
